**Run graph removal before projection.**

The ordinary-quad example is not the failing case because frozen ordering places an equal default-graph row before its named-graph row. However, `surface_of` emits ordinary rows before reifier and annotation rows. A valid dataset can contain an ordinary named-graph `rdf:reifies` quad and a default-graph reifier row with the same `(s, p, o)` values. The named row inserts the projected default triple, then the later default side-table row removes it.

`query_rdflib` accepts `default_graph`, passes it into `QueryMode::dataset`, and therefore can reach this branch with `scope.1 = Some(g)`.

Remove all excluded rows before inserting selected projections.

<details>
<summary>🐛 Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
--- "a/bindings/python/src/py_store/quad_store.rs"
+++ "b/bindings/python/src/py_store/quad_store.rs"
@@ -82,19 +82,22 @@
         if !scope.0 {
             selected.withdraw_named_graph_declarations();
         }
-        for quad in purrdf_core::ir::QuadValues::surface_of(&dataset) {
-            let include = scope.2 || quad.g == scope.1;
+        for quad in purrdf_core::ir::QuadValues::surface_of(&dataset) {
             if (!scope.0 && quad.g.is_some()) || (scope.1.is_some() && quad.g.is_none()) {
                 selected.remove(&quad);
             }
-            if include && (scope.2 || scope.1.is_some()) {
-                selected
-                    .insert(purrdf_core::ir::QuadValues::triple(quad.s, quad.p, quad.o))
-                    .map_err(|error| {
-                        PyValueError::new_err(format!("query graph selection failed: {error}"))
-                    })?;
+        }
+        if scope.2 || scope.1.is_some() {
+            for quad in purrdf_core::ir::QuadValues::surface_of(&dataset) {
+                if scope.2 || quad.g == scope.1 {
+                    selected
+                        .insert(purrdf_core::ir::QuadValues::triple(quad.s, quad.p, quad.o))
+                        .map_err(|error| {
+                            PyValueError::new_err(format!("query graph selection failed: {error}"))
+                        })?;
+                }
             }
         }
         selected.freeze().map_err(|error| {
             PyValueError::new_err(format!("query graph selection failed: {error}"))
         })
```

Add a regression test with a named ordinary `rdf:reifies` quad and a default reifier row that project to the same triple, then query context `g`.

**🎯 Functional Correctness** | **🟡 Minor** | **⚡ Quick win**

**The iterative walk can accept an on-demand read through `Apply`, but the recursive reference refuses it.**

For a non-optional policy, the `Apply` arm reuses `Resume::Join { pattern, left }`. `Resume::Join` calls `join_read`, which returns the right operand's `OneCall` unchanged when `left` is an empty BGP. As a result, `CallReadShape::of` can accept an on-demand call read under a contextual application.

That read ignores `policy.inputs`, `row_pipeline`, `group_domain` and `reduced_adjacent`, so it can return rows that the `Apply` evaluator would never produce. The recursive reference at lines 5745-5758 always returns `Err(not_one_call("a contextual application"))`.

The two walks therefore disagree. The randomized differential test does not catch this because its generator never builds `Apply`. Refuse the read in the iterative walk for both policies, and keep the provenance merge.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

Add a dedicated resume variant:

```diff
-                frames.push(WalkFrame::Resume(if policy.optional.is_some() {
-                    Resume::LeftJoin
-                } else {
-                    Resume::Join { pattern, left }
-                }));
+                frames.push(WalkFrame::Resume(Resume::Apply {
+                    optional: policy.optional.is_some(),
+                }));
```

```rust
Resume::Apply { optional: is_optional } => {
    let (right_columns, _) = pop_result(results);
    let (left_columns, _) = pop_result(results);
    let columns = if is_optional {
        optional(left_columns, right_columns)
    } else {
        conjunction(left_columns, right_columns)
    };
    (columns, Err(not_one_call("a contextual application")))
}
```
</details>

**Keep optional `Apply` right-hand endpoint uses indirect in every endpoint summary.**

When `policy.optional` is present, `classify` treats the right operand as indirect. The `ServedIndex` `GraphPattern::Apply` summary still merges both operands as direct. A parent `served_at` lookup can therefore treat a right-hand `SERVICE ?endpoint` as served even though the optional operand is not required to carry it. Apply the same policy-sensitive rule to the summary and recursive reference paths.
